issues.description: Indentation bug: the version guard is placed at module scope but visually attached to Math_unary's signatures list, breaking the class body and the registration.
issues.detail: In mathdecl.py the `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` block immediately follows the `signatures = [...]` list inside class Math_unary. Read carefully: the blank line and dedent end the class, but the conditional `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` only runs the decorator after class construction. This is correct only by luck of dedentation; one stray space silently re-enters the class. State the invariant in a comment or move the guard to a clearly top-level block.

issues.description: Missing `import sys` in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py where `sys.version_info` is now referenced.
issues.detail: The diff adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` to both mathimpl.py files but only imports `sys` in mathdecl.py. If `sys` is not already imported in those modules, import will fail on every Python version. A reader cannot verify correctness without seeing the import; the literate form requires the dependency be visible at the top.

issues.description: Inconsistent version-gating mechanism: typing uses `sys.version_info`, tests use `PYVERSION`. Pick one.
issues.detail: numba already exposes `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` (the test file imports it). Using `sys.version_info` in production modules and `PYVERSION` in tests creates two sources of truth for the same predicate. A future Python-version bump must be audited in two notations. Use `PYVERSION` consistently, matching the rest of the codebase's convention.

issues.description: No test of correctness against `math.exp2` reference values; `run_unary` likely compares to pyfunc but edge cases (very large/negative, integer overflow boundaries) are absent.
issues.detail: Tests reuse `exp`'s x_values verbatim: `[-2,-1,-2,2,1,2,.1,.2]`. Tests catch what proofs miss only if the inputs exercise the algorithm. exp2 has interesting behavior at integer powers (exact results), at denormals, and at overflow (~1024). Add at least one integer power, one near-overflow, and one negative-large value to verify the LLVM intrinsic matches CPython semantics.

The diff explicitly notes `\ No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files end with a newline; many doc toolchains and linters complain. Trivial fix; flagging because literate artifacts should be clean.

issues.description: Lost blank line before `@infer_global(math.atan2)` reduces readability of the class boundary.
issues.detail: The original had two blank lines separating Math_unary from the next decorated class (PEP 8 for top-level definitions). The diff replaces that whitespace with the conditional, leaving one blank line. Minor, but Knuth's first law: write for the reader. Restore the blank line and place the conditional in a clearly delimited block with a one-line comment explaining the gate.

review.summary: The change is small and the algorithm is trivial — `math.exp2` is delegated to the `llvm.exp2` intrinsic — so there is no complexity claim to audit and the data-structure choice is forced. The patch is UNDER-AUDITED at the seam between Python-version availability and module-load-time decoration: `sys` is referenced without being imported in two impl files, and the version gate is expressed two different ways (`sys.version_info` vs `PYVERSION`). The test reuses `exp`'s inputs without exercising exp2's interesting points (exact integer powers, overflow at ~1024, denormals near -1074), which is exactly the case Knuth warns about — proved-correct by delegation, not tried-correct on the boundary. Fix the imports, unify on `PYVERSION`, add a one-line comment stating the invariant ("registered only on 3.11+ because math.exp2 was added then"), and broaden the test inputs. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.
